before taking the startup mutex, preserves relative/spaced output paths and
child exit codes, and bounds preview execution to 30 seconds. Normal startup,
startup-splash rendering and updater routes retain their behavior. Other
arguments remain rejected, with bounded JSON-escaped argument details in both
the log and error. Startup logging now includes version/count/arguments.

Windows x64 / .NET Framework 4.8 / Python 3.12.14: both binaries compiled. Three
isolated bootstrap checks passed using real synthetic child processes, covering
all forwarded modes, quoting, relative paths, exit status, preserved startup and
helper command routes, and bounded/escaped diagnostics. All 23 settings checks

## Terminal mouse routing (issue #7) — 2026-10-16

Implemented on `7-breaking-and-entering-camera-turret-not-working`, based on
main `696421f` merged at `093e30f`. On Windows x64, a bounded isolated run
of the supported US XBE reproduced the Breaking and Entering terminal failure:
player mode was `0x2000`; physical mouse movement changed hidden player angles
while the active console pointer stayed fixed. The user confirmed the terminal
menu pointer, rather than a selected camera view, was blocked. Disassembly of
US `sub_003700D0` identifies local-index console ownership, pointer coordinates,
4–251 bounds, inactivity reset, scripted input and pause gates.

The shared `src/interface/pc_terminal.h` now routes counts to that pointer and consumes
terminal input without changing player angles, including invalid transitions.
Coordinates stay in the game's logical space, independent of screen resolution,
FOV or aiming inversion. Windows and SDL adapters use the same helper.
The guarded-memory regression and full MSVC x64 Release build passed on Windows,
including patch-stack validation and the real Windows adapter regression in
`tests/input/pc_controls.c`. The user confirmed physical pointer movement, but left-click initially still
sent Fire instead of the terminal's Confirm action. The follow-up shared input
context and `0940-terminal-mouse-select.patch` now suppress the
normal left-button binding while selecting and emit A/Confirm. A held button
must be released across either transition to prevent accidental selection or
firing. Windows regression covers the native adapter-to-binding path with bounded synthetic input; the shared
fixture covers click state, and the native SDL fixture has equivalent checks.
The updated MSVC x64 Release build and native checks passed, including Confirm
without Fire and release-before-fire on terminal exit. All 27 patch tracking/
transition cases passed (the historical-upgrade fixture was updated to exclude
this new dependent overlay, then rerun). The shared terminal regression passed.
The user confirmed the final physical playtest: pointer movement, left-click
camera selection, and ordinary aiming/firing after leaving the terminal work.
The read-only capture also records return to mode `0x2` with no active terminal.
Native Mac compilation/execution remain
unverified; see MAC-001.

## Issue 19 decal projection (2026-10-16)

- Source: decal fix on `19-floating-decals` (this revision), based on
  `696421fd080a5bd57cb894b76302080f59f52485`; pinned runtime `d90c929` and
  checksum-verified US XBE. Windows x64 build 26300, MSVC 19.42.34435.0,
  Python 3.14.2, CMake 4.4.4, D3D11.
  Release executable SHA-256:
  `ada6ab457f3369c64c89d3a46f4d6ed29a698e5a3861364d876b6076e0e6048d`;
  multiplayer identity `85180d72`.
- Cause: the two decal render paths independently reconstruct a depth-biased
  perspective matrix, bypassing the adjusted camera. A baseline 1920x1080
  Arcade capture used horizontal scale `1.440737` for biased effects versus
  `1.080552` for the widened scene. The fixed capture uses `1.080552` for
  both, retaining the distinct depth terms `-0.10050558` and `-0.10000556`.
  This corrects the guest projection rather than changing HUD classification.
- Validation: the complete patch stack applies; supported `tsfp.ps1 -Action
  Build` regeneration/build and all native build tests passed. Executable seal
  and game-content verification passed. The decal, cinematic and patch-transition
  suites passed (35 cases; one historical fixture was updated and its failing
  case rerun). Wrapper checks cover both decal callers, default/wide/ultrawide
  and cinematic apertures, unchanged depth and other callers, missing camera,
  guest return state, and both Windows/native display build flags.
- Live check: a bounded Hotel Arcade match at 1920x1080 with no bots reached
  gameplay; fired wall impacts stayed aligned while strafing and rotating the
  camera. No crash or unresolved-call report occurred. All save, input and both
  display configuration routes were isolated under `private/decal-validation`.
  Selected screenshots and captures remain ignored there; disposable partition
  images were recycled after the runs. Personal settings and saves were preserved.
- Remaining checks: other Arcade maps, explosion impacts, split screen, and live
  default/4:3/ultrawide rendering were not exercised. Mac source uses the same
  wrapper, but native build/rendering and other-device synchronization remain
  unverified. See [MAC-010](MAC_PORT_BACKLOG.md#mac-010--in-game-resolution-preview-and-rollback).

## Native interpolation mesh-layout repair — October 15

- Investigated the user's missing first-mission terrain/character screenshots.
  Found a shared replay-state bug: vertex declarations changed during a guest
  frame, but interpolation retained neither those changes nor the initial
  declarations. Replaying with the final layout could misread vertices or skip
  a draw entirely. Immediate-mode effects temporarily use a sixteen-float4
  layout, then return to their normal stream layout.
- Added `0750-interpolation-layouts.patch` after the existing patch stack.
  It snapshots active declarations at frame start and copies successful layout
  changes into the replay in order, preserving the final guest state. The native
  executable was rebuilt; temporary culling/depth/CPU diagnostic edits were
  removed. No generated game C was edited.
- Before the fix, a moving first-level guest/midpoint pair showed fire/smoke

## Native frame-time investigation and upload fix — October 15

- Confirmed the reported slowdown on `mac-port`. Measured host-present intervals
  in the stationary first-level canyon, 120–145 seconds after the first present,
  excluding menus, loading, the opening animation and CPU sampling. Three bounded
  150-second runs used the same isolated profile and menu input sequence.

  | Run | Average FPS | Median frame | 95th percentile | Worst frame |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | Before, rotating captures enabled | 14.63 | 68.34 ms | 71.61 ms | 80.61 ms |
  | Before, captures disabled | 14.85 | 67.28 ms | 70.48 ms | 74.60 ms |
  | After, rotating captures enabled | 60.00 | 16.44 ms | 19.09 ms | 33.80 ms |

- Captures were not the main cause. CPU sampling placed 1,442 of 1,942 main-thread
  samples in `glBufferSubData`, including driver waits for earlier GPU work.
  The renderer reused offset zero in one transient vertex/index buffer on every
  draw. Replacing each buffer's storage with `glBufferData` lets the driver retain
  earlier uploads while the GPU finishes them. The follow-up sample has no
  `glBufferSubData` calls. CPU vertex interpretation remains a performance limit.
- Compiler settings stayed unchanged to isolate this fix: Debug game code and
  the runtime libraries' existing `-O2`. `BUILD.json` now records the build type
  and complete configure command. The result is specific to this scene and Mac;
  it does not establish 60 FPS throughout the campaign or monitor scanout pacing.
- Added opt-in `--profile-frames` (20,000 CSV rows maximum, no GPU readback) and
  a frame-statistics tool that selects a known gameplay interval. The corrected
  1,500-frame measurement had one interval over 33.33 ms and none over 50 ms.
- Added real-GPU coverage for 128 queued, changing vertex/index uploads before
  readback, including nonindexed draws and both 16/32-bit indices. All graphics,
  input and three native CTests pass; portable tests: **17 passed, 2 Windows-only
  checks skipped, 7 subtests**. The read-only native launcher check passes.
  The final timed run reached at least 7,800 guest frames and host presents,
  with no native fault or sampled GL error. Reviewed the world/weapons/HUD capture.
- Test partition images were recycled; personal saves/settings were not used.
  Evidence: `logs/native-frame-performance-validation.json`,
  `logs/mac-perf-*.csv`, `logs/mac-perf-*-sample.txt`,
  `logs/mac-frame-fixed-build.log`, `logs/mac-frame-portable-tests.log`, and
  `private/captures/native-mac/native-frame-performance.png`.

## First native Apple Silicon execution — October 15

- Built `build/macos/futureperfect_recomp` as a native ARM64 Mach-O executable
  on macOS 27.0.1 with Apple Clang 21, Python 3.12 and the shared pinned runtime,
  Python dependencies and SDL submodule. No Wine, Rosetta or Windows process

  imports, initialized the game's graphics device successfully, loaded game
  assets, ran worker threads and completed at least 1,800 guest frame calls.
  No native fault was recorded. The runner stopped it at the time limit;
  SIGTERM did not exit within the three-second grace period, so it used SIGKILL.

  reserves one 4 GiB virtual range and maps only its own unused pages; all 28
  low-RAM aliases, contiguous memory, device apertures and tiled alias mapped.
  It does not weaken macOS protections or overwrite unrelated host mappings.
- Implemented native relative/absolute and periodic waitable timers, and an
  ARM64 signal handler for supported scalar MMIO loads/stores. Protected NV2A
  interrupt writes and AC97 reset writes have real-signal regression coverage;
  unsupported instructions stop with diagnostics instead of being skipped.
  Read/write aliases let handlers update device backing without opening the
  protected guest page to concurrent writes. APU accesses use the existing
  device model, whose DSP implementation remains incomplete upstream.
- Implemented POSIX sparse partition images with the existing retail geometry,
  partition-device path routing, volume-directory opens and relative file opens.
  Existing image contents are preserved. These fixed the guest's early request
  to return to the Xbox dashboard. Isolated title metadata was created under

  wall-clock fallback rather than claiming a hardware playback cursor. Movies

  at `~/.config/xboxrecomp/titles/45410066.conf`. Its newly created default was

  PowerShell tests skipped, 7 subtests passed. Fresh application, upgrades,

  pass. The actual Windows executable was not rebuilt or tested on this Mac.

  This runs natively. The initial low-address-linker
  experiment was terminated before useful output; the passing test uses the
  normal executable layout and OS-selected addresses. It does not establish
  that the full Xbox address-space mapping is ready.
- The native path-routing source passes a Clang syntax check. The memory-layout
  and kernel-bridge sources still fail on Windows process-affinity/timer APIs.
  Further source review found Windows-only title startup/graphics hooks,
  missing POSIX HLE audio/input implementations, an incomplete OpenGL renderer,
  a Windows-wired Vulkan backend, and Linux `.so` names in the non-Windows
  FFmpeg loader. Native game boot, rendering and gameplay are **not built or
  verified**. No platform support claim is inferred from the upstream README.
- Portable checks: 8 passed, 2 Windows-only PowerShell tests skipped, 7 subtests
  passed, using Python 3.12 and pinned pytest 9.1.1. Native evidence is in
  `logs/native-platform-before.*`, `logs/native-platform-after.*`, and
  `logs/native-kernel-compile-summary.json`. Personal saves and settings were
  not used. No disposable virtual disk images were created.

## Display settings and texture preview — October 15

- The working build now adds **Display settings** through the US game's own
  button builder in main Settings and paused Options. Resolution selection,
  Apply, Keep and Revert all use guest menu widgets and navigation.
- 1080p, 1440p, 4K and monitor-reported modes are offered. Rendering targets and
  depth buffers resize live; a 15-second unconfirmed preview returns to the old
  resolution. Confirmed settings persist beside the PC input configuration.
- The US camera wrapper updates the perspective matrix and horizontal CPU
  frustum together. The HUD retains its proportions in a centered 4:3 region.
  Front-end menus retain the original layout. Fullscreen remains Alt+Enter.
- The actual-menu replay verified 1080p apply/save, 1440p preview, timeout
  rollback, and return to the original menu. Native tests cover resolution
  bounds, monitor-mode deduplication, failed allocation handling at the API
  boundary, aspect calculations and persistence. Original game files, saves
  and keyboard/mouse configuration passed 424 protected-file hash comparisons.
- First-mission runs rendered 3840×2160 and 3440×1440 scene buffers and reached
  paused Options without a recorded crash or unresolved indirect call. The
  resolution checks use GPU render targets on the available display; a physical
  ultrawide monitor, split screen, and a full campaign are not validated.
- The expanded texture preview contains 11 replacements, approximately 44 MiB,
  covering selected terrain, masonry, timber, concrete, floor tiles, metal panels
  and one weapon atlas. Four replacements loaded in a 174-second opening-mission
  run at 1920×1080; gameplay and paused Options were reached without a recorded
  crash or unresolved call. The remaining seven need scene-specific runtime checks.
- DDS files have complete mip chains: two 4096×4096, eight 2048×2048, and one
  2048×1024. Square source art is 1254×1254; stone masonry is 1774×887. These are
  resampled outputs, not native 4K generated art. A character draft shifted facial
  and ear UV details and was kept out of the active pack.
- The coverage audit tracks 5,547 supported texture keys: 11 installed, one draft
  requiring correction/review, and 5,535 awaiting art. Another 753 cataloged
  payloads use unsupported formats. Embedded textures may remain undiscovered.
  This is not a completed game remaster. Eight offline tool tests pass; installed
  DDS hashes, dimensions and mip chains pass the audit. All 427 protected game,
  save and settings files matched their pre-test hashes; temporary disks and
  frame captures were recycled. Exact new prompts and real source sizes are saved.
- Pack compilation enforces the user's 6 GiB cap including metadata. Runtime
  replacement residency remains capped at 512 MiB. The supported-asset size plan
  is approximately 2.5 GiB before source art and unsupported-format additions;
  the plan is not completed artwork or a guarantee of final full-game size.
- Runtime changes are reproducible from the pinned upstream revision using
  `0230-pc-controls.patch`, `0330-save-routing.patch`, and `0340-texture-pack.patch`; the last
  patch includes the renderer wiring shared by display and texture features.
  Fresh application in setup order and repeat-build checks pass.

## Interactive launcher correction (2026-10-15)

Normal play now launches through `tools/play.py`, which waits for the game and
writes its output directly to `logs/play-*.out` and `logs/play-*.err` using native
file handles. Interactive runs disable the generated code's default 400,000-line
function trace; diagnostic profiling remains available through SmokeTest.
The previous PowerShell GUI launch could return before the game, and inherited
or redirected output could stall startup. The corrected normal launch produced
captured startup logos and advancing swaps, with keyboard/mouse configuration
loaded. The user also confirmed that the logos appeared. Main-menu and gameplay
interaction for this hardware playtest is still to be tried.

## PC controls menu (2026-10-15)

Added a PC Settings → Keyboard & Mouse entry to the native game window's menu
bar, with F2 access in windowed and fullscreen modes. The owned settings dialog
lists all 24 Xbox actions with four keyboard/mouse binding slots each, mouse
sensitivity, inversion, mouse enable/disable, defaults, and Cancel. Capture
supports keys, five mouse buttons, and wheel directions; conflicting assignments
can be moved after confirmation. F1/F2/F9–F11 and Windows keys are reserved.
Gameplay input is blocked while editing, but simulation is not paused: pause
the mission first.

Saving applies bindings and mouse options immediately. Polls copy an immutable
binding snapshot under an SRW lock; editor input cannot become gameplay input.
Configuration changes preserve other ports and unrelated JSON members. Writes
use a temporary sibling file and atomic replacement, retaining the previous
configuration as `.bak`; failed writes retain the active bindings. Build checks
use a separate default fixture so user-customized bindings do not affect tests.

Validation: native input and save-path suites passed, as did the new settings
suite for live sampling, persistence and fresh-process reload, backup, unrelated
JSON retention, read-only failure, invalid values/reserved keys, defaults, native
dialog Cancel, key/wheel capture, and conflict reassignment. The UI was rendered
and visually inspected. A bounded real-game integration check verified both
entry points, F2 in fullscreen, input ownership/return, rendering after closing,
and that Cancel left the user's file unchanged. Both patches reproduced all
seven modified upstream files from pristine pinned sources. Evidence is in
`logs/pc-settings-release-validation.log` and `logs/pc-settings-game-tests.log`.

## Pickup range comparison fix — October 16, 2026

Issue [#6](https://github.com/TheDoffman/timesplitters-future-perfect-pc/issues/6):
the US pickup tick at `0x000C15B0` compares the original radius squared with
horizontal distance on two paths (`COMISS xmm3,xmm0` and `COMISS xmm0,xmm1`).
At their shared branch, `0x000C17D9`, the translator discarded the differing
operand states and emitted `if (_flags)` with `_flags` initialized to zero.
The horizontal rejection therefore never ran. Eligibility and vertical checks
still ran, explaining early pickups rather than indiscriminate item grants.

`patches/compiler/0300-recomp-float-joins.patch` merges SSE comparison snapshots across those
paths, retaining their original ordered/unordered conditions. Pickup radii,
weapon grants and input bindings are unchanged. No generated game C was edited.
`tools/build/recomp-generation.py` records generator source hashes; Windows Build
regenerates stale C, while native Mac requests `--generate`. The normal Windows
Test command includes the new regression. Existing generated checkouts migrate
on their next build.

edits were preserved. The fix is isolated on `fix-pickup-range` over newer main for the user-requested push. No binary release is included.

was verified before generation and execution. Host: Windows x64, Python 3.12.14,
MSVC 19.44.35224.0, Release, Direct3D 11.

Validation:

## Automatic runtime patch tracking — October 16, 2026

Implemented on `fix/automatic-patch-tracking`, based on main `979a16c`, for
commit and publication at the user's request. Each successful loader invocation
records exact patch bytes, SHA-256 hashes, order and context options in the
runtime's per-worktree Git metadata (`tsfp-patches.json`). The next invocation
unwinds that recorded stack before applying the current branch's stack, so
removed, renamed or edited patch files no longer require a manual archive.
Existing runtimes bootstrap through the active/legacy recognition path once.
Branches need the updated loader to maintain this record.

The entire transition is validated on disposable source copies. Invalid records
and conflicting edits fail before runtime writes. Concurrent source/record edits
observed during validation are preserved. Failed source writes or metadata
publication roll back source changes and retain the old record. Successful
records are replaced atomically; repeated no-op runs do not rewrite metadata.
No game data, generated C or build tree is duplicated.

Validation on Windows 11 x64 10.0.26300, Python 3.12.14, MSVC 14.44.35207,

  `625769a2fdfa5497a5bdf735b960f5c3100882d3d3b6b68389f515877e04176a`, identical to

shared stream adjustment now includes headroom alongside mix-bin/3D attenuation;
it still falls back unchanged outside the checked XDK layout. A new regression
fails before this correction and passes afterward, including a headroom change,

### Follow-up: stale music packets at level transitions (2026-10-16)

The user's headroom-build retest still had harsh distortion. A bounded,
read-only capture attached to their human-controlled Windows playtest (PID 7616,
headroom executable `c645c07a...`) isolated a separate fault. Music stream slot
266 retained three old 73,728-byte packet addresses across the menu-to-story
transition. Their memory now contained unrelated game data. Respectively
1,642, 1,605 and 1,770 of 2,048 stereo ADPCM headers were invalid; independent
decoding clipped 16.04%, 13.48% and 18.30% of samples. Captured host PCM matched
that corrupted input. The next five music packets had valid headers and no
clipped decoded samples. Captured cutscene/dialogue PCM matched its source.
Earlier probes only saved the 22,042 Hz story streams, missing this 32 kHz
music stream. Reducing headroom could not repair its corrupted input.

The shared adapter intercepted ordinary Flush but neither FlushEx nor Release.
The pinned XBE's stream stop routine calls FlushEx with zero timestamp and ASYNC;
its Release method can destroy the stream while the host still retains packets.
The new `0030-dsound-stream-lifecycle.patch` retires the host voice and packet model
only on final Release, preserving non-final references and allowing the allocator
to reuse the same interface address with fresh format/queue state. It handles
immediate FlushEx and zero-time ASYNC (packet callbacks completed in DoWork),
blocking submission/status completion while the asynchronous flush is pending.
Other scheduled/envelope FlushEx modes retain the existing XDK fallback and
remain outside this fix's validated scope.

Three lifecycle tests reproduced stale host queues before the hooks; 17 audio
cases passed after the initial implementation. The async regression also checks
that intervening GetStatus/Process calls cannot complete cancelled packets from
the wall clock. Build discovery initially missed the new HLE wrappers, producing
unresolved original-body symbols. `tools/build/recomp-generation.py` now fingerprints
HLE export/original/import declarations, with a regression for addition/removal
and body-only edits. Wrappers are regenerated from source, never edited by hand.

Read-only inspection did not modify the running process, inputs, personal
settings or saves; the user navigated and closed the game. Captures are capped
at 12 MiB and 240 seconds in ignored `build/issue-8-audio/live` with source/PCM
metadata and analysis. Current local rebuild and post-fix listening results are

- Online source-build integration: a new network-menu entry, HTTPS browser with
  certificate fingerprint checking, public/private rooms, compatible-only
  listing/joining, peer credentials and leases, and a virtual-address bridge
  using the game host's forwarded UDP port. Guests establish outbound paths;
  the host relays guest-to-guest traffic. Two local instances used Online and
  an HTTPS directory to join a 2/16-player lobby and enter the same Shrink match.
  Cross-internet routing and full-match stability remain unverified. Campaign
  co-op remains a separate future effort.
  Automatic hosting now detects public IPv4 over HTTPS, starts/stops a local
  directory with the bridge, reuses its certificate and offers a copyable
  invitation containing the directory address, fingerprint and join code.

- Experimental PC System Link: native framed UDP, strict build/content identity
  checks, default-protocol discovery sockets, and XNADDR/key mapping. Two isolated
  game instances discovered a match, joined a 2/16-player lobby, and loaded into
  the same Thief match. This is a same-PC loopback test, not a cross-network test
  or a completed-match validation. See [multiplayer status](../players/multiplayer.md)
  for the later Online integration and remaining cross-network validation.

  `tools/textures/texture-formats.py` verifies the pinned executable SHA-256, dispatch
  instruction bytes and all eight case immediates before using this mapping.

configuration values. The prior sampled change from 1.1 to approximately 0.55
was not evidence of live damage. Original damage routine `sub_000BA310` changes
entity `0x1CC` (health), `0x1D0` (armor), `0x1D4` (last damage tick) and clamps
against `0x1D8` (maximum health). Current packets and diagnostics use those
fields. The earlier claimed health proof is superseded.

allowlist, restore living bots' `0x61` drawing/collision flags instead of drawing

it through the original Arcade constructor when a living host snapshot arrives.

shooter, preventing the remainder of death and scoring. The guest meanwhile
could apply damage/death locally and subsequently have HP restored by a host
snapshot. The new separate `pc-network-bot-authority` patch permits the host
to finish configured NPC deaths and prevents a guest from predicting them.

own NPC health, corpse/respawn visibility and each NPC's victim score column.

snapshots hide stale replicas and weapons; damage-acceptance bit `0x10` now
travels with the drawing/collision mask. Guest kill announcements follow
confirmed score-column increases and do not replay death side effects.

## Issue #118: Online bot session ownership (2026-10-18)

Local, uncommitted on `118-bug-online---guests-unable-to-see-bots`, based on
`6d351c4`. Reproduced with two Windows instances using the actual Online menu,
companion processes and authenticated UDP bridges, backed by an isolated
loopback directory. Two humans and six bots loaded the same match. Host bots
became active; guest bot bodies retained disabled flags and initial health,
then disappeared as the original game removed their unsynchronized bodies.

The host generated and registered its local XNKID, but never resolved its own
XNADDR: Online deliberately does not relay discovery broadcasts to their sender.
Bot transmission incorrectly required that self-discovery cache entry. Bounded
diagnostics confirmed `peers=0, targets=1` on the host, so every snapshot returned
before sending. The guest's host address and match context were correct.

`src/network/pc_network.c` now retains the local session ID from XNetCreateKey, enables
it on matching XNetRegisterKey, and uses it directly for bot snapshots. Foreign
registration/unregistration does not change ownership. Matching unregister,
new key creation and transport shutdown invalidate the preceding registration.
The guest still checks the selected host, session ID, match, state validity and
tick ordering; the Online bridge's authentication and compatibility checks are
unchanged. No snapshot format, generated game code or patch-stack change.

Validation on Windows AMD64, Python 3.14.2, MSVC 19.42 / toolset 14.42.34433,
with the D3D11 game renderer:

- Verified the supported US `default.xbe` SHA-256
  `3cfd001a84fc3e08175d6c4b2e42ebf49577a089b5d0bd87ac724f61a41816bc`.
  Physical free space before builds was approximately 458 GB; apparent sparse
  test-disk capacities were not treated as physical allocation.
- The native regression reproduced the old host's missing Online snapshot,
  then passed with the fix. It covers send without a self-XNADDR cache entry,
  receipt through the bridge into a smaller title buffer, rejection of wrong
  source/session/match, unrelated registration, unregister/re-register,
  replacement keys and disconnect/reconnect. Existing LAN transmission passes.
  Logs: `logs/issue118-regression-before.log` and
  `logs/issue118-regression-after.log`.
- `tsfp.ps1 -Action Build` applied/verified the complete pinned patch stack and
  passed its native checks. Logs: `logs/issue118-build.log` and
  `logs/issue118-final-build.log` (completed optimized native regressions).
- All 43 selected Online, identity, bot model/guest/native-fallback,
  original-US results and patch transition/tracking checks passed across the
  initial run and focused rerun. One initial patch test encountered WinError 32
  while cleaning its temporary source fixture; the isolated rerun passed.
  Logs: `logs/issue118-tests.log`, `logs/issue118-patch-recheck.log`.
- In the rebuilt Online match, all six guest bot bodies received drawable flags

### Khallos sky follow-up: source assets and independent pixel samples

At `244ee77` on the same Mac, both captured sky texture payloads matched their
full 262,144-byte originals in `pak/storymem/l_11_stm.pak` (archive entries
`caa402f6` and `68d16bdb`), as well as the two related cutscene-memory archives.
No texture replacement, truncated upload or stale cache content was found in
these two resources. The sky mesh duplicates vertices at UV boundaries:
connected, nondegenerate triangles have maximum UV edge length about 0.171,
not the large jumps suggested by inspecting consecutive vertex records alone.
A diagnostic capture with wrapped UVs produced no visible correction and was
not turned into a runtime workaround.

An independent Python calculation of perspective-correct UVs, Morton texture
unswizzling, bilinear sampling, vertex-color modulation and the captured blend
state matched all 65 sampled interior sky pixels within one 8-bit channel
value on KosmicKrisp. This checks these samples against the captured arguments;
it does not establish that the guest submitted the same scene/state as an
original Xbox or a known-good PC build. Local calculation and result:
`logs/sky-reference-samples.py`, `logs/sky-reference-result.json`; source-byte
comparison: `logs/sky-asset-check.py`. No game assets were added to Git.

The sky remains visually unverified. A known-good matched scene is still
needed to distinguish an upstream scene/state error from the original low
resolution artwork and its intended appearance. A blanket wrapping, fog or
brightness change is unsupported by the evidence collected so far.

### Shared scene interpolation and Khallos pacing (2026-10-19)

The commit carrying this section on `codex/shared-scene-interpolation` depends
on `codex/khallos-sky` at `683026d` and the unmerged shared-renderer stack.
Both title entry points now configure projection c60 and transform c64-c75
through `src/graphics/tsfp_interpolation.h`. The shared recorder recognizes
programs reading composed transforms such as c68. The HLE patch deprojects
these matrices, interpolates their recovered affine motion and reapplies the
projection; it does not substitute unrelated/stale c64 values. Replay scheduling
also accounts for preparation time and refreshes the clock before drawing.

### Vulkan portability texture swizzles (2026-10-19)

The commit carrying this section on `codex/vulkan-portability-swizzle` depends
on `codex/shared-scene-interpolation` at `f1f4236` and its unmerged renderer stack.
The shared Vulkan device enabled `VK_KHR_portability_subset` but never queried
or enabled its optional `imageViewFormatSwizzle` feature. Alpha-only and
opaque-X texture views consequently violated Vulkan's portability requirements.
The additive `vulkan-portability-swizzle.patch` queries and explicitly enables
that feature, preserving the custom-border-color feature chain; an unsupported
portability device now gets a clear prerequisite error instead of invalid views.
Native Vulkan devices without the extension retain their existing feature path.
This follows the [Vulkan feature-enabling contract](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPhysicalDevicePortabilitySubsetFeaturesKHR.html).

The shared D3D11/Vulkan resource contract now samples A8, BGRX, R8 and RGBA
textures and verifies all channels. Before the fix, the new MoltenVK test
reproduced two swizzle validation errors even though its sampled pixels matched.
After the fix, both pinned Mac drivers passed the expanded resource/pixel tests
and production frame replay with no validation errors. The historical patch
upgrade fixture excludes this dependent patch from its pre-Vulkan starting
state, then checks installation of the complete stack. Relevant source checks:
75 passed and three host-specific skips across the initial run and focused
retest. Windows D3D11 execution and GitHub CI have not run for this change.

## Issue #167 - Experimental smoother presentation (2026-10-19)

Windows implementation is local and uncommitted on `feature/167-144-fps`, based
on `d63a156`, with the complete patch stack on pinned upstream `d90c929` and
the supported US XBE hash checked before each build/test. This adds 120/144 FPS
host targets while retaining the 60 Hz guest clock and normal game speed.
Input and simulation still update at the game's rate; this does not establish
native 120/144 Hz input response.

The Windows renderer previously configured only the fixed c60 projection, so
extra presents could repeat the same pose. It now configures TSFP's c64-c75
camera/object transforms. A rational clock keeps the fractional 144/60 phase,
drops expired deadlines, and omits replaced guest endpoints from Shown. Gate
interpolation alone reached the target in menus but often fell back to 60 during
gameplay. The final implementation also predicts from the two completed poses
during guest CPU work, bounded to one guest interval. Three frame histories plus
a transient state-only snapshot, separate prediction color/depth buffers, and
held real-frame feedback images preserve the partial guest frame. During CPU
prediction, clears/draws into shared effect textures or custom depth targets
are skipped while the main scene continues; failed/unknown targets still
disable prediction. Cuts, failed
matches, movies and slow frames retain a guest fallback. Prediction can produce
corrections; CPU-deformed effects and screen-space UI retain their original rate.

The launcher exposes experimental Smooth motion targets and a separate supported
fullscreen monitor refresh selector. Existing interpolation and desktop-rate
preferences remain the defaults. `Play-Smooth.cmd` provides a temporary 144 FPS
override (`120` selects 120 FPS) without saving settings. Supported monitor modes
retain desktop dimensions and are restored on focus loss/exit. The existing crash
helper also provides independent process-death restoration. Mock adapter tests
cover supported/unsupported modes, focus/normal/abrupt exits, failed recovery and
preservation of independent user mode changes. The opt-in physical test skipped
cleanly: this session exposes a virtual 1920x1080@60 display with no supported
120/144 Hz mode, despite the GPU's physical-monitor WMI report. Its desktop mode
remained unchanged. Physical high-refresh scanout/restoration and subjective
smoothness require testing on the user's local display.

### Performance settings audit and user adjustments (2026-10-19)

Still local/uncommitted on `feature/167-144-fps` at base `d63a156`. Runtime
source and the tested game binary above are unchanged in this follow-up; no
additional measured engine FPS gain is claimed. The audit found three setup
gaps: selecting a target could leave VRR disabled, users could subsequently
select incompatible game pacing, and the scale UI implied supersampling still
applied with an explicit output resolution. In fact, `pc_display_scene_size`
overrides the scaled console dimensions with the chosen output size.

### Stability and recovery audit (2026-10-19)

Local/uncommitted on `feature/167-144-fps`, base `d63a156`. The audit found two
recoverable failures in the current high-refresh work:

- Refresh restoration treated a failed `EnumDisplaySettingsW` query as if the
  user had independently changed the display. It cleared pending restoration
  and disarmed the crash watchdog. `src/interface/pc_refresh.c` now retains both until
  the mode can be inspected, restored, or confirmed to have changed separately.
  The failure-injection test failed before the fix and passes after it; it also
  verifies failed restoration, subsequent success and watchdog event state.
- A single failed extra render-target acquisition permanently disabled
  interpolation. Its callers then calculated redraw costs from the previous
  successful present timestamp. The additive `interpolation-recovery.patch`
  returns an explicit success result, keeps failed draws out of timing/counters,
  and restores prediction state before returning. Windows 120/144 targets use
  normal guest frames and retry at most once per second, allowing recovery
  without restarting. Legacy/native disable-on-failure behavior is preserved.
  Tests exercise failure and recovery in the real interpolation implementation,
  all three scheduling paths, cooldown allocation throttling, guest-present
  fallback, unchanged timing/slot counters and preserved guest recording/state.

## 2026-10-20: launcher texture installation and OneDrive path repair

Branch fix/launcher-onedrive-paths, based on main 5db4efc. The local portable
installation had no Textures folder and logged zero replacements. An attempted
directory junction was rejected by the launcher. After the user removed that
junction, a normal directory with 2,484 NTFS file hard links (1,242 DDS plus
metadata) was installed. Same-file identity was verified for every pair: no
second texture payload copy. The subsequent user-run session logged 45 loaded
replacement entries and Enhanced mode. This establishes loading, not visual
approval or complete remaster coverage. Future new/replaced keys need an explicit
installation refresh; hard links are not a directory mirror.

A separate path-validation defect also rejects ordinary OneDrive ancestors:
Core.PathIn rejects every reparse marker, including a measured Cloud Files tag
0x9000601a. The Windows adapter now reads metadata without following the final
reparse point and admits only the documented CLOUD / CLOUD_1 through CLOUD_F tag
family. Unknown tags, junctions and symbolic links remain rejected. Installation,
download and cleanup guards share this decision; missing-file checks retain
dangling-link inspection. Reference: Microsoft Reparse Point Tags documentation,
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/reparse-point-tags.

Validation on Windows x64: build-launcher.ps1 -Test passed all groups, including
109 updater regressions, existing real junction-cleanup guards, cloud/unknown-tag
cases, download/recovery, settings, sessions and maintenance. The built launcher's
PathIn accepts the actual desktop installation's Bin, Textures, settings and
pending-download paths; it positively identifies the desktop's Cloud Files tag.
13 Python launcher/handoff tests plus 26 subtests passed. No game build or new
automated playtest was needed. The original installed launcher rejected
these paths in a read-only probe. After the user closed the game and launcher,
the corrected binaries and self manifest were installed locally on October 20.
Installed SelfUpdate.Complete and GameSettings.StartInfo passed in the Windows
.NET Framework runtime, resolving all 1,242 DDS files. Nine personal settings
files and the game build manifest retained their hashes. A small launcher-only
recovery copy and installation receipt remain under .launcher/local-fixes.
This local fix has not been published as a launcher release. Personal settings and saves remain
untouched. Local build output is build/launcher-onedrive-fix in the working root.

Mac: no adapter is required for Windows Cloud Files. The existing Mac rejection
of filesystem links remains unchanged behind its platform adapter; native Mac
build/interaction validation was not performed in this Windows-only repair.

## Launcher v1.3.1 release preparation (2026-10-24)

Prepared from main `aed726e1` on `release/launcher-v1.3.1`. Advances the shared
version and numeric assembly attributes to ship existing launcher improvements:
60/120/180/240 FPS Beta presets, capture-health reporting with bounded gameplay
breadcrumbs in diagnostic exports, and launcher-specific release changelogs.
The FPS/capture features require compatible game runtimes; this release contains
only launchers. Optional texture delivery and Classic/Enhanced controls remain
as implemented in v1.3.0. Package paths, update manifest names and one ZIP per
platform remain unchanged. No personal files or game assets are modified.

Validation is pending below and in the release PR/workflow. Windows and Mac
must both pass the existing build, behavioral and package checks before public
upload. Mac Developer ID signing/notarization remains unavailable, as documented
in the release publisher. No gameplay validation is claimed by a launcher build.

Local Windows x64 validation passed using .NET Framework 4.8 and checksum-pinned
artwork: the complete `build-launcher.ps1 -Test -RequireArtwork` suite, all 31
publisher regressions, backlog consistency, repository-context validation and
whitespace checks. Build output is isolated in ignored `build/l131`; logs are
under this source worktree's ignored build directory. Hosted Windows/Mac checks
and exact public-package verification remain release gates.

## Two-body collision impulse contract (2026-10-25)

On `test/native-vehicle-contact-acceptance`, extended the existing original-US-XBE
rigid-motion fixture rather than tuning physics from the variable live pillar
route. No production runtime, geometry, coefficients or executable changed.
`native_rigid_motion.c` now lifts original166060 in addition to1667C0/16FC00 and
checks 432 isolated frictionless two-body impacts against a separate double
precision generalized impulse equation. Both bodies have distinct masses and
existing spin; cases vary three-dimensional normals, lever arms, diagonal and
rotated positive-definite world inverse-inertia tensors, approaching/separating
motion, Original60/native120/144/180/240 and an extra0.7ms secondary step.

The checks compare relative point velocity, both force impulses and both torque
impulses, including conservation of total linear/angular impulse about the world
origin. Largest measured component error in the focused run is0.000000649 at a
0.00001 absolute bound. Independent mutations remove the second mass contribution
or its torque response and must fail in the new cases. The complete existing
vehicle timing file passes all19 tests in56.64s, retaining its clock, RNG,
secondary-step, sleep/wake, steering, camera and other regression mutations.

Original16DF60 damage/effect notification is a checked service boundary after
force accumulation. This test observes a single impulse before integration and
drag; it does not supply terrain broadphase, deterministic live controls,
frictional contacts or a complete vehicle collision replay. It narrows the
low-level response uncertainty and provides a regression contract; it does not
prove live handling parity or rule out collision-selection/integration defects.
Both-host CI already selects this test file, but original-routine checks require
the private supported XBE and skip in asset-free CI. Physical Mac validation
remains open under MAC-060. No private assets/generated guest code are tracked.


## Forced/damped material scrolling at native rates (2026-10-25)

On `fix/native-material-motion`, the original127500 material update exposed an
arithmetic rate dependence beyond its earlier cache/timing gate. The authored
step damps/adds force to velocity, then moves U/V using that updated velocity.
Fractional Euler steps change the product and the travel sum. A held-force test
without drag gives U0.614500 at Original60 versus0.608501 at120 after two seconds
(about0.006 texture repeats less travel); original constant-velocity-only tests
did not cover this case.

Shared `pc_native_material.h` and five numeric sites now split the complete
velocity/travel affine map in raw time at current game speed. Damping, held
forcing and travel are normalized together; zero/weak damping have stable limits.
Original mode, whole/catch-up raw time, pause and unsupported/nonpositive decay
bases retain original arithmetic. Original force-table samples, force clamp, UV
wrapping, image/resource/event order, material layout and saves stay owned by the
original routine. This advances fresh material state, not rendered-frame blends.
Varying within-tick force sampling and complete visual parity remain separate.

The asset-free helper passes180 fractional partitions against an independent
one-step recurrence. The original surface/cache fixture checks48 normal/quarter
speed schedules at60/120/144/180/240 and mixed intervals with held forcing/drag,
plus pause and exact original fallback. Independent controls remove damping,
forcing or travel normalization and must fail. Full timing/vehicle suites pass
115 tests in229.77s; the final test-only expansion adds exact fallback checks
and its eight focused tests pass again in22.11s. The forced/damped controlled
case reaches about0.000003 maximum U/V error rather than the previous0.006.
GPU calls in that fixture are spies; this does not prove live varying forces.

Supported Windows build and bundled checks pass on base40600133 with executable
SHA256 `3e24f6f93f4f95734902d559885db62627f343dbafda174a0713e57a3b569999`.
Bounded Scotland runs at native240, native120 and trueOriginal60 pass movement,
pause/resume, canonical signed profile preservation and owned-process cleanup.
Reviewed native captures show the path, weapon, scenery and NPC. The integrated
read-only native120/Original60 censuses each retain40 observations identifying
one active material with forcing0.002, drag0.007 and direction(-0.6,0.4). All40
native samples have positive fractional raw time and equal frame brackets. This
establishes activation/identity, not coherent completed-update or pixel parity.
The first late standalone census could not open the already-closed240 child;
it records zero rows and is rejected evidence. The rerun attaches at owned-child

## TREE callback fractional phase gate (2026-10-25)

An audit of remaining whole-game-tick entry gates identifies original US
`sub_001D88B0`. Initializer1D8A10 finds the TREE-tagged entity, initializes active
state/phase and registers this callback at1D8A94. The callback initially reads
4E7944 only as a zero-time gate, then overwrites EAX with entity state. Its
phase at entity+1A4 advances with float4E794C divided by ticks-per-second; its
pose at+C8 is derived directly from that phase using the original exponential.
It emits a crossing event near phase1 and a terminal effect/clamp at80, clears
active state, and multiplies E0 by the original-0.1 factor.

The original whole-tick gate discards fractional intervals even though its body
integrates fractional time. A fixture executing the original routine reproduces
phase0.25 after one game second at native240, with no phase1 event yet. The
unchanged-policy regression fails its one-second phase check (including native
slow-time schedules) before the repair. Changing only the audited gate to test
positive live float time makes phase advance correctly at60/120/144/180/240.
Original mode retains its original gate; carried whole fields remain unchanged.
The adjacent1D8AB0 callback has per-call additions and is deliberately outside
this change pending its own integration audit, not assumed safe from proximity.

`tests/gameplay/native_tree_motion.c`, selected by existing `test_native_timing.py` on
both CI hosts, translates/executes the pinned private US routine rather than a
rewritten phase model. Two effect services are spies; other original arithmetic,
branching, loads/stores and stack operations execute. Exact constants are read
from the verified XBE, including complete x87 doubles. Forty rate/slow/phase
schedules verify phase and analytic pose, one crossing/one finish with event-time
bounds, pause (including stale carried ticks), terminal clamp/state/retirement,
unchanged clock words and preserved callee-saved registers/stack/x87 depth.
Whole/catch-up sequences produce identical entity bytes/event counts in native
and Original modes. A negative control replacing only the generated gate load
with its original value must fail; no generated game file is edited.

The asset-free `native_timing_guest.c` clock fixture additionally checks ten
rate/slow schedules, one-second phase accumulation, unchanged neighbor sites,
pause and Original fallback on both hosted platforms. This policy test does
not stand in for original pose/event execution when private-XBE cases skip.
The two focused checks pass4.50s. All117 timing/vehicle checks pass231.84s;
21 repository/backlog checks pass3.35s. The supported Windows rebuild and bundled
checks pass, producing executable SHA256
`a35525a76633b3d99d7571b1b9efdef9faad443739ae905ae4e7938a588b3690`.
Repository context/index and whitespace checks pass. No private assets or
generated game sources are committed. Live registration/activation/rendered TREE behavior,

## TRAP solver mixed-clock repair (2026-10-25)

runtime/transition/PR validation and launcher compatibility checks. This related
TRAP audit/fix stays in that same PR; no new PR is created.

Initializer1D8C40 finds the TRAP-tagged entity, sets+C0=-88/+E0=0/state1A0=0,

inside it, the sine-table force adds a fixed50-times-sine impulse to+E0 once
per call, while+C0 motion and phase+1A4 consume converted whole game ticks.
It emits one sound/control request, clamps/bounces at90 with the authored-0.1
factor, increments a discrete counter and removes the callback beyond11.

Broad native conversion substitutes the current fractional frame interval at
1D8AF5(phase) and1D8B6A(travel), even though the gate still selects whole-tick
calls and their fixed impulse. The resulting impulse/time mismatch changes
motion, phase and event progression. An original-routine fixture fails before

states). A naive always-open gate is independently rejected because it adds
extra fixed impulses even with the corrected converted spans.

original integer gate and fixed impulse/lookup/clamp/retirement logic stay
unchanged on positive intervals. A pause-only override rejects a stale whole
count when live game time is zero. Clock words are never rewritten. Other
continuous conversions, including neighboring sites, continue to use live
fractional time. There is no new adapter, save field, retained per-entity cache,
solver coefficient or RNG policy.

solver, not a claim that TRAP now supplies a fresh fractional pose each native
frame. Its rendered motion cadence still follows the original solver calls.
Smooth fractional trap motion needs a separate coupled integration/presentation
investigation that preserves the verified impulse/event behavior; opening the
gate alone is not that solution. The overall native-refresh goal stays open.

sine-table initialization and original12010 sine helper, using constants from

## Native multiplayer (2026-10-30)

Draft PR [#416](https://github.com/TheDoffman/timesplitters-future-perfect-pc/pull/416),
branch `feature/mac-online`, based on main `cc531ea9` and updated through
`d73758d3`. Implementation is pushed for review, not a published release. The Windows primary audio checkout was untouched.
The isolated Apple Silicon worktree uses the same-host runtime/game cache.

- Shared native transport and Xbox address/error/memory adapters compile on
  Windows and macOS 27.0.1 ARM64. Windows focused networking/UI tests: 38 passed,
  1 skipped; Mac: 36 passed, 3 platform-specific skips. Added real browser
  host/join/cancel checks: 3 passed on each host. Additional Windows package,
  patch-ledger and CI-scope checks: 122 passed (includes those three browser cases).
- The actual Mac game executable's `--online-self-test` passed host, join and
  cancel through `pc_online_connect`, returned to SDL, stopped/reaped the child,
  and left no directory lobby. These are supervisor checks, not title gameplay.
- A native C fixture linked to the production transport exchanged a framed
  payload from the Windows machine to the physical Mac and back over LAN.
  Both validated the same fixture compatibility ID. This is packet interoperability,
  not proof of complete game-build compatibility or a played match.
- Mac game generated from the verified supported US XBE and built natively.
  A 45-second bounded unlocked-profile boot recorded at least 2,400 guest frames
  and 2,400 successful Vulkan presents, no native fault, no shader compile failure
  and no Vulkan validation errors. Saves/settings were isolated and disposable
  disks cleaned by the normal runner. Full campaign/gameplay acceptance is separate.
- The 65 MiB relocated Online runtime passed actual Python, Tk 9.1, TLS,
  certificate generation, CA-store and themed-window checks. Native dependencies
  have local loader paths and ad-hoc signature verification. It uses CPython 3.12.12,
  pinned cryptography/cffi/pycparser wheels, and original license/source metadata.
  Build-host Tk support was added without upgrading its existing Python interpreter.
- Remaining acceptance: complete native/native and Windows/Mac matches, bot
  movement/combat/respawns, reconnect/rematch behavior, Internet/router forwarding,
  and visual Dock review. A complete distributable game release was not published.
  Source users must build matching Windows/Mac revisions and content; installed
  older Windows releases will intentionally reject the new compatibility identity.

Local evidence: `logs/mac-online-*.log`; Mac `logs/native-boot-summary.json`,
`logs/mac-online-adapter.log`, `logs/mac-online-lan.log`, `logs/mac-online-bundle.log`.
